What is a transactional email service? A transactional email service sends messages that a customer expects after an action: a password reset, purchase receipt, booking confirmation or account update. Your application supplies the recipient and message; the service handles sending and delivery reporting. Newsletters, promotions and audience campaigns belong in Email marketing. Should I send transactional email with SMTP or the Email API? Choose SMTP to keep your application’s existing message-building code. Choose the Email API for structured request fields and published templates, with access through Bird’s SDKs, CLI and hosted MCP. Both use the same sending infrastructure, domain verification, suppression handling and reporting. Does a delivered transactional email mean it reached the inbox? Delivered means the receiving mail server accepted the message. Inbox Insights estimates inbox and spam placement from seed accounts and a measurement panel. Scale without losing control. The Free plan includes the sending allowance shown above. Choose a paid plan when you need more capacity, and review its included sends and additional-usage rate. How do I compare paid email plans? Compare the monthly allowance, plan charge, overage rate and features you need. The volume table shows published rates so you can estimate both a typical month and a busier one. Are dedicated IPs included? Dedicated IPs are a separate monthly add-on for eligible email plans. Check the Dedicated IP pricing page for the rental and setup considerations. Does an email plan include SMS, WhatsApp or mailboxes? An email sending plan covers its email allowance. Other channels and mailbox capacity have separate pricing and should be estimated separately. What happens to unused capacity and overage? Unused monthly sending capacity does not roll over. Additional emails use the published overage rate. The default overage ceiling is five times your plan; sends pause at the ceiling unless you agree different terms. What is included in my plan? Plans include authentication, dashboards, suppression, webhooks, 30-day retention and a shared sending IP. Dedicated IPs are a separate add-on for Growth and above. Put it into practice. Products On this page Email overview Send transactional and marketing email through POST /v1/email/messages . Use a bk_{region}_... key with its matching regional host: https://us1.platform.bird.com or https://eu1.platform.bird.com . We sign the message with DKIM, deliver it, and report each recipient's outcome. To send something before reading further, the quickstart takes you from an API key to a delivered message. This page covers the model the rest of this section assumes, and points at the guide for each part of it. How sending works A send is accepted in one call and delivered asynchronously. POST /v1/email/messages validates the payload and sending domain, then returns 202 Accepted with an em_ message ID. Read each recipient's outcome through webhook events or the message endpoints. Sending email covers the payload, field limits, and response. Two consequences of that model shape the rest of this section. One message, many recipients, one lifecycle each. A message to five addresses produces five independent outcomes, and the message-level status you read back is an aggregate over them. Suppression is evaluated the same way: one suppressed address comes back rejected while the other four deliver. Every message declares why you are sending it. A category of transactional or marketing decides which suppressions apply to it. Someone who unsubscribed from your newsletter still needs their password reset to arrive, and the category is what tells us the difference. A send can also arrive by another route, or leave later. SMTP accepts submissions from anything that speaks the protocol, and scheduled sending holds a message until a time you set. The Email section of the dashboard Email is one of the channels in the dashboard sidebar. Its pages, in the order they appear: Page What it holds Onboarding A three-step checklist: create an API key, send an email, add your domain. It shows until you have finished it Metrics Delivery, open, bounce, and complaint rates over time; see Email metrics Emails Every message sent; see the email log . Its Receiving tab lists what came in Mailboxes Programmable inboxes your code reads and replies from; see Agent mailboxes Templates Reusable subject and body content, with a draft and published versions; see Email templates Domains Your sending domains, their DNS records, and live verification status; see Sending domains IP Pools Dedicated IPs and the pools they sit in; see Dedicated IPs and pools Broadcasts One email to a stored audience, with delivery tracked per recipient; see Broadcasts Suppressions Addresses we do not send to, and why; see Suppressions Unsubscribe page Branding for the hosted page every marketing email links to; see Unsubscribe links SMTP Connection settings, per-key send defaults, and live connections; see SMTP Recipients live outside the Email section, in Contacts in the sidebar: All contacts stores people with typed custom properties (see Contacts ), and Audiences groups them into the reusable lists a broadcast sends to (see Audiences ). Where each guide fits Sending. Sending email is the one to read first: it owns the payload every other send path is a variation on. From there, templates store content you reuse, attachments add files, batch sending submits up to 100 messages in one request, and broadcasts send one email to a whole audience. Domains and authentication. Sending domains covers registering a domain and getting it verified. DKIM, SPF, and DMARC explains what each record proves to a receiving mailbox provider, and BIMI shows your logo beside your messages in email apps that support it. Reputation. Suppressions is the list of addresses we stop sending to, filled automatically from hard bounces and complaints; unsubscribes stop delivery the same way but through a stated preference instead of a suppression record. Dedicated IPs and pools and IP warmup cover sending from IP addresses only your organization uses. Email deliverability ties those together. Knowing what happened. The email log shows one message and its per-recipient timeline. Email metrics aggregates your traffic. Events is the event vocabulary and how webhooks deliver it to your own endpoint. Receiving. Receiving email covers both ways in: a forwarding address we generate that needs no DNS, or MX records on a subdomain you own. Agent mailboxes builds on that with inboxes your code sends from as well as reads. Testing. The mail sandbox exercises your integration end to end without delivering anywhere. Send to bounce@messagebird.dev to generate a hard bounce through the real event and webhook pipeline. The test writes nothing to your suppression list. To move production email from another provider, follow the migration guide . It covers request mapping, DNS, suppressions, webhooks, sandbox testing, and traffic cutover. zh.summary: 提供邮件、消息和语音接口，让开发者把通信接到应用与代理。
zh.judgment: 优势应在可交付的通信和运营支持，AI 接口便利不能代替可靠送达。
zh.replaces: 开发团队分别接通信供应商，处理认证、路由、送达与回调。
zh.product: 官网覆盖邮件、短信、WhatsApp、语音等，并提供 MCP、CLI 和开发资料。它是通信平台，可被 AI 代理调用，不能将整个既有业务写成新生 AI 助手。
zh.customer: 开发者、应用企业与消息量较大的运营团队是用户。付费需求来自必要通信与稳定服务，不一定来自用户对 AI 标签的兴趣。
zh.workflow: 应用或代理通过接口发消息，再由路由、送达状态与 webhook 接回业务。身份、退订、失败重发和状态记录是交付链的重要部分，本次未发送消息。
zh.business_model: 邮件价目有每月 1000 封免费额度、Startup 每月 15 美元起和 Growth 80 美元起，并列额外发送费。不同套餐功能不同，邮件价格也不能套到语音或 WhatsApp。
zh.traction: 官方客户页面与文档可核验，未取得独立送达、留存或完整收入对照。案例证明通信有实际应用，不证明每个 AI 接口都形成新增付费。
zh.moat: 运营网络、发送信誉、渠道连接和开发生态可能形成优势。其他通信 API 与直接渠道接入是替代，切换成本应与实际服务质量一起比较。
zh.funding_read: 此记录是债务融资，不能解释成股权轮次或新增收入。资本结构与渠道投入需分开看，稳定现金流和服务经济比 AI 宣传更重要。
zh.risks: 渠道规则或发送信誉变化可能影响送达，额外用量和多渠道会增加费用。代理若误发或重复发送，也会放大客户支持与信誉负担。
zh.takeaway: 把通信动作、送达状态和业务回执连起来。让代理调用复用成熟通信基础设施，并保留可控发送与失败处理。
zh.watch_next: 看送达质量、每类通信成本、客户续用与支持负担。单独跟踪 AI 工具接入是否增加长期有效流量。

en.summary: Communication APIs connecting email, messaging and voice to applications and agents.
en.judgment: Dependable delivery and operations matter more than convenience of an AI interface.
en.replaces: Integrating providers separately and handling identity, routing, delivery and callbacks.
en.product: The site covers email, SMS, WhatsApp and voice with MCP, CLI and documentation. It is a communications platform usable by agents, not an entirely new personal assistant.
en.customer: Developers, application businesses and high-volume operations teams are users. Essential communication and stable service drive payment, not necessarily interest in an AI label.
en.workflow: Apps or agents send through APIs, with routing, delivery status and webhooks returning to business processes. Identity, opt-outs, retries and records complete delivery; no messages were sent.
en.business_model: Email pricing lists 1,000 free monthly sends, Startup from $15 and Growth from $80, with overages and different features. Email fees cannot be transferred to voice or WhatsApp.
en.traction: Official cases and documentation were reviewed without independent delivery, retention or revenue comparisons. Existing communications use does not establish additional paid AI adoption.
en.moat: Operations, sender reputation, channels and developer ecosystems could be defensible. Other APIs and direct channel integration compete on effective quality and switching effort.
en.funding_read: This is debt financing, not equity or new revenue. Capital structure and channel investment are distinct; dependable cash-flow economics matter more than AI promotion.
en.risks: Channel policies or reputation can change delivery, while overages and channels add cost. Mistaken or repeated agent messages increase support and reputation burden.
en.takeaway: Connect send actions, status and business receipts. Reuse mature communication systems for agents with controlled sending and recovery.
en.watch_next: Watch delivery, channel cost, renewal and support. Separately assess whether agent integrations add useful recurring traffic.
